title: Hello World | Marker
content_html:
In the early 1960s, to prove the F-1 rocket engine wouldn’t shake itself apart on the way to the Moon, Rocketdyne engineers put bombs inside it.

Combustion instability had been destroying engines on the test stand for years. The fix was not drawing up a cleverer design: it was a test.

Detonate a charge inside the chamber mid-burn and if the engine could swallow the explosion in a fraction of a second, it passed. They ran that gauntlet until instability had nowhere left to hide. When the first Saturn V flew in November 1967, every stage succeeded live on the first try, and it worked because the ground testing had been merciless enough to earn it.

The world we trust is built this way. I came up through nanoengineering and medical device research where a single dust particle ruins a wafer. Richard Feynman is credited as the godfather of nanoscience. A couple years back I found a quote he had said about the Challenger disaster that I feel applies to all safety-critical technology:

“For a successful technology, reality must take precedence over public relations, for nature cannot be fooled.”1

In AI terms: demos, claims, and benchmark scores do not matter if the system fails in production. Testing is what turns an invention into infrastructure.

Breaking things for a living

I spent years in the autonomous vehicle industry. My honest job description was: break things before the world does. Zoox went straight at the hardest problem: Level 5 autonomous urban point-to-point transportation of humans. The theory is that if that can be solved, then package delivery or suburban transport will be addressable with the same technology.

That left me with a conviction to build testing discipline on the most safety-critical version of problems. If your voice agent safely handles legal questions and SSNs, the same stack can likely be trusted to take a pizza order.

The gap

When I left AVs to build voice AI, I expected the hard part to be the agents, but it was knowing whether they worked. Voice is audio, telephony, interruptions, accents, latency, and a model that answers differently every time you call it.

Pieces exist for testing but are largely unconnected. Simulations here, transcripts there, a judge prompt someone tuned once and never versioned. Despite the shift to improvement loops, if context leaks at the seams, agent quality slips.

Marker closes these gaps. An operating system for voice agents built on tightly connected primitives. Every simulation, transcript, judgment, and fix carries its full context and version history. Every piece is native to both AI and human operators. Everything is configurable, durable, and plugs into whatever stack you already run, wherever you run it.

Why “Marker”

A marker is a primitive: the surveyor’s stake, the trail flag, the small durable thing you place so you can find your way back. That’s what verification evidence should be.

But a marker is also a creative instrument, the thing you sketch and iterate with as you form your ideas. We wanted to capture the essence of evidence and authorship in one word.

Voice is the future of how people interface with software. This future doesn’t arrive because demos get better. It arrives when it is safe to fail: a place where an agent can blow up a thousand times on the test stand so it never blows up in production. Rocketdyne got to the Moon by bombing its own engines. We want to hand you a platform where you can place bombs within your voice agent.

If you want the ultimate safety infrastructure for your agents, we’re building it at usemarker.ai. Say hello.

Test as you fly, and fly as you test.

— NASA systems-engineering principle

  1. Richard P. Feynman, “Personal Observations on the Reliability of the Shuttle,” Appendix F to the Rogers Commission Report, 1986. nasa.gov/history/rogersrep/v2appf.htm

content_html_zh:
20 世纪 60 年代初，为了证明 F-1 火箭发动机在前往月球的途中不会自行解体，Rocketdyne 工程师在发动机内部放置了炸弹。

多年来，燃烧不稳定一直在毁坏试验台上的发动机。 解决方案并不是制定更聪明的设计：而是进行测试。

在燃烧过程中引爆燃烧室内的装药，如果发动机能在不到一秒的时间内吞掉爆炸，那么爆炸就通过了。 他们接受了挑战，直到不稳定无处可藏。 当第一架土星五号于 1967 年 11 月飞行时，每个阶段都在第一次尝试中就成功了，而且它之所以成功，是因为地面测试足够无情，才赢得了它。

我们信任的世界就是这样建立的。 我通过纳米工程和医疗设备研究发现，单个灰尘颗粒会毁掉晶圆。 理查德·费曼被誉为纳米科学的教父。 几年前，我发现他在谈到挑战者号灾难时说过一句话，我认为这句话适用于所有安全关键技术：

“对于一项成功的技术来说，现实必须优先于公共关系，因为大自然是不会被愚弄的。”1

用人工智能术语来说：如果系统在生产中出现故障，演示、声明和基准分数并不重要。 测试是将发明转化为基础设施的过程。

以打破东西为生

我在自动驾驶汽车行业工作了多年。 我诚实的工作描述是：抢在世界之前打破一切。 Zoox 直接解决了最困难的问题：5 级自治城市点对点人类交通。 理论上来说，如果这个问题能够得到解决，那么包裹递送或郊区运输将可以使用相同的技术来解决。

这让我坚定了针对最安全关键版本的问题建立测试纪律的信念。 如果您的语音代理可以安全地处理法律问题和 SSN，则可以信任同一堆栈来接受披萨订单。

差距

当我离开自动驾驶汽车去构建语音人工智能时，我预计最困难的部分是代理，但真正重要的是知道它们是否有效。 语音是音频、电话、中断、口音、延迟以及每次呼叫时应答不同的模型。

存在用于测试的部分，但基本上没有连接。 这里是模拟，那里是笔录，法官提示某人调整过一次，从未版本化。 尽管转向了改进循环，但如果上下文在接缝处泄漏，代理质量就会下降。

标记弥补了这些差距。 基于紧密连接的原语构建的语音代理操作系统。 每个模拟、记录、判断和修复都带有其完整的上下文和版本历史记录。 每一件作品都是人工智能和人类操作员原生的。 一切都是可配置的、耐用的，并且可以插入到您已经运行的任何堆栈中，无论您在何处运行它。

为什么是“标记”

标记是一种原始的东西：测量员的木桩、小路旗、你放置的小而耐用的东西，这样你就可以找到回去的路。 这才是验证证据应该有的样子。

但记号笔也是一种创意工具，是您在形成想法时绘制和迭代的工具。 我们希望用一个词来捕捉证据和作者身份的本质。

语音是人们与软件交互方式的未来。 这个未来不会因为演示变得更好而到来。 当可以安全地失败时，它就会到来：一个代理可以在测试台上爆炸一千次的地方，因此它永远不会在生产中爆炸。 火箭达因通过轰炸自己的发动机到达月球。 我们想为您提供一个平台，您可以在其中在语音代理中放置炸弹。

如果您想要为您的代理提供终极安全基础设施，我们正在 usemarker.ai 上构建它。 问好。
